samples.text:
Nowadays, many people work very long hours, and even when they go home, they continue to think about their work. This situation creates problems for these workers and also for their families. In this essay I will discuss these problems and suggest some solutions.

The first problem is for the health of the workers. When people work too much and do not rest, they feel stressed and tired all the time. Some of them cannot sleep good at night because they are worrying about their tasks for the next day. After a long time, this can cause serious illness such as depression or heart problems. The second problem is for the family. If parents come home late and always check their emails, they do not have time to play with their children or to talk to their partner. Children may feel that their parents does not care about them, and couples can have more arguments.

There are some solutions for this problem. Firstly, companies should not expect workers to answer emails or phone calls after working hours. Secondly, employers can give more flexible hours, so that people can finish work earlier or work from home some days. Thirdly, workers themselves should learn to relax, for example by doing sport, having hobbies or switching off their phones in the evening. It is also important that they plan their free time with their family, like having dinner together everyday.

In conclusion, long working hours and thinking about work all the time cause stress and health problems, and it also damage family relationships. I believe that both companies and workers should take action to have a better balance between work and life.
samples.why: Problems for individuals and families plus solutions all addressed · ideas relevant but general · clear paragraphing with mechanical linking · adequate vocabulary with awkward phrasing · errors in adverbs, agreement and word form.

samples.text:
In today's competitive working environment, many employees put in long hours and find it hard to switch off from work, even at weekends. This essay will discuss the effects of this on individuals and their families and propose some possible solutions.

For individuals, the most serious consequence is the damage to their physical and mental health. Working long hours without proper rest leads to chronic stress and fatigue, and people who constantly think about unfinished tasks often have trouble sleeping. Over time, this can result in burnout, anxiety and even conditions such as high blood pressure. Ironically, overwork can also reduce productivity, as exhausted employees make more mistakes and find it harder to concentrate. The effects on family life are equally significant. Parents who arrive home late and spend the evening answering emails have little time or energy left for their children, who may miss out attention and guidance. Partners, too, may feel neglected, and tension over work commitments is a common source of conflict in relationships.

There are several ways in which this situation could be improved. Employers should take the lead by making it clear that staff are not required to respond to messages outside working hours, and some governments have even introduced a legal right to disconnect. Flexible working arrangements, including remote work and adjustable start times, could also help employees to fit their jobs around family responsibilities. On a personal level, individuals can set firmer boundaries, such as turning off work notifications in the evening and scheduling regular time for exercise and family activities. Managers should also lead by example, because staff are unlikely to switch off if their boss sends emails at midnight.

In conclusion, excessive working hours harm people's health and put pressure on family relationships. Supportive workplace policies, combined with healthier personal habits, would help employees achieve a more sustainable balance.
samples.why: Clear position · effects on individuals and families extended and supported · solutions from employers and individuals logically presented · good collocation (switch off, set firmer boundaries) · one preposition slip.

samples.text:
For a growing number of employees, work no longer ends when they leave the office. Long hours, combined with smartphones that keep them permanently reachable, mean that professional concerns now spill into evenings, weekends and holidays. This essay examines the toll this takes on individuals and their families, and suggests how a healthier balance might be restored.

For the individual, the absence of genuine recovery time is profoundly harmful. The mind needs periods of detachment to recover from sustained effort, and when these are lost, stress accumulates into chronic exhaustion and, eventually, burnout. Disrupted sleep is a common early sign, as people lie awake rehearsing tomorrow's deadlines. Paradoxically, the pattern is also counterproductive for employers, since fatigued staff tend to be less creative, more error-prone and more likely to take sick leave or resign. The impact on families can be just as damaging. Children whose parents are physically present but mentally preoccupied may feel that they come second to a screen, and the everyday rituals that sustain family life, from shared meals to bedtime conversations, are gradually squeezed out. Between partners, an unequal burden of household responsibilities can breed resentment.

Addressing the problem requires change at both organisational and personal levels. Employers can set explicit policies discouraging out-of-hours communication, and several countries have legislated a right to disconnect, giving employees legal protection when they choose not to respond. Realistic workloads matter just as much, because a ban on evening emails achieves little if the volume of work cannot be completed within normal hours. Leadership culture is decisive here: when senior staff visibly protect their own time, others feel permitted to do the same. Individuals, in turn, can create clear boundaries, such as disabling work notifications and reserving certain times for family and leisure.

In conclusion, overwork undermines health, productivity and family relationships. Sensible workplace policy, backed by leaders who model balance and individuals who guard their personal time, offers the most realistic solution.
samples.why: All parts fully addressed with well-developed, perceptive ideas · solutions qualified and prioritised · skilful cohesion and paragraphing · natural, precise vocabulary (detachment, squeezed out, breed resentment) · error-free range of structures.
